Summary

Technical advisory to scope migration and AI enablement for Catalyst Planet, with quotes from developers who have a presence in the US. Advisory until 15 November 2026 is provided free of charge. Subsequent to that the work required will be between 5 and 10 hours to finalise the quotes and provide the recommendations. I will bill this at a discounted rate as a fixed £1,000 and we aim to have the quotes and recommendations completed by the end of the year.

Deliverables

2 × Next.js + Sanity quotesTwo written quotes from developers or studios with a presence in the US for building the site on Next.js, with Sanity as the content editor.
1 × WordPress quoteOne written quote from a developer or studio with a presence in the US for building the same site on WordPress.
Comparison and recommendationA side-by-side of price, timeline, what each includes and leaves out, and the running costs of each platform, with my recommendation.
Advisory throughoutCalls and messages as needed through the period: questions on the quotes, the developers and the choice between platforms.

Not included

  • Building, designing or hosting the website
  • Managing the chosen developer once the build starts
  • The developers' own fees, which are agreed directly between you and them

Agreement terms

Once signed by both parties, this quote is the agreement between the Client and Fohm (the Supplier) for the advisory above.

  1. Scope and changesThe Supplier delivers the deliverables above. Anything outside them, such as more quotes, other platforms or managing the build, is a change request: the Supplier confirms the cost and timeline in writing before starting, billed at £250 an hour.
  2. Free advisory periodAdvisory until 15 November 2026 is free in line with our current engagement.
  3. Client responsibilitiesThe Client gives the information needed for the brief, answers questions within 5 working days, and confirms it has the rights to any content shared with developers.
  4. PaymentInvoices are due within 14 days. The Supplier may pause work while an invoice is overdue, and may charge interest and compensation on late payments under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998.
  5. Third-party developersThe developers who quote are independent of the Supplier. Their quotes, prices, timelines and work are their own, and any build contract is made directly between the Client and the developer. The Supplier is not responsible for a developer's quote, performance, delays, security or quality, or for any loss arising from them. The Supplier takes no commission or referral fee from developers.
  6. AdviceThe Supplier gives its advice with reasonable skill and care, based on the information available at the time. The decision on which developer and platform to use, and its consequences, rest with the Client.
  7. OwnershipOnce paid, the Client owns the brief, comparison and recommendation, and may share them with anyone. The Supplier keeps its general know-how and templates.
  8. LiabilityEach party's total liability under this agreement is limited to the fees paid under it. Neither party is liable for indirect or consequential loss, including lost profits or revenue. Nothing here limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or for anything else that cannot be limited by law.
  9. TerminationEither party can end this agreement at any time with 7 days' written notice, or immediately if the other materially breaches it and does not put it right within 7 days of being told. If it ends after 15 November 2026, the Client pays for the paid work done to that point (at £250 an hour, up to the £1,000 fixed fee) and, once paid, receives everything produced so far.
  10. ConfidentialityEach party keeps the other's non-public information confidential and uses it only for this work. The brief is shared with the developers approached, with the Client's agreement. The Supplier may name the Client and describe the work in general terms in its portfolio unless the Client asks it not to.
  11. Independent contractorThe Supplier works as an independent contractor and chooses how the work is done.
  12. Events outside controlNeither party is liable for delays caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including developers not responding, provided it tells the other party promptly.
  13. GeneralThis document is the whole agreement and replaces earlier discussions. Changes are only valid in writing (email is enough) agreed by both parties. Notices are given by email to each party's usual address. If any clause is unenforceable, the rest still applies. Neither party may transfer this agreement without the other's written consent. This agreement is governed by the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction.
